questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Provide you with an escape route.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position keeps you out of other vehicles' blind spots, helps you see and be seen, helps you avoid hazards, and gives you an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: In New York State, an operator is legally intoxicated at a blood alcohol content (BAC) of _____ or higher.
questions.explanation: In New York State, anyone with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher is considered legally intoxicated and cannot operate a motor vehicle.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten the bike, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes hard while leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the bike, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly in a curve, first straighten your motorcycle and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten the bike, apply the brakes smoothly, reduce your lean angle, then increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: When riding at night, your following distance should be:

options.text: The same as during the day.

questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances at night because you lose visual clues like shadows and light contrasts. You should keep a longer following distance when riding at night than during the day.

questions.question: Approved helmets:

options.text: Allow you to see as far to the sides as needed.
Do not have to be worn if you think they limit your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow you to see as far to the sides as needed.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that helmets limit their vision, but this is not true. An approved helmet lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways as you cross.
Always come to a full stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white downward-pointing triangle is a yield sign. Slow down and be prepared to yield to pedestrians or vehicles in the crossroad. You may need to stop. Proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can the body eliminate per hour?
questions.explanation: On average, the body can eliminate about one drink per hour. The time needed varies by person, so it is safest not to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire powers the bike, so you lose acceleration.
The flat tire shakes the bike, making mirrors hard to use.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because it affects your ability to steer. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely exit the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: A proper lane position can help you do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.

questions.explanation: Your lane position affects several safety factors. It helps you avoid other drivers' blind spots, increases your ability to see and be seen, and sets you up for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: In New York State, outside of New York City, you may _______ when you see a solid red traffic light at an intersection.
questions.explanation: In New York State, outside of New York City, you can turn right at a red light. You must stop completely first. You must also let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first. In New York City, you can only turn right on red if a sign says you can.

questions.question: Signs that show where services are located look like:

options.text: Blue signs with white letters or symbols
Green signs with white letters or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue signs with white letters or symbols
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters and symbols. These signs tell you where to find rest areas, gas stations, campgrounds, and hospitals.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Stay in the tire tracks left by other cars
Stay in the center of your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the tire tracks left by other cars
questions.explanation: The center of a wet lane is slippery and dangerous. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by other cars. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: To lean your motorcycle when turning, you should:

options.text: Push the handlebar opposite the direction you are turning
Push the handlebar in the direction you are turning

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handlebar in the direction you are turning
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make it lean, push the handlebar in the direction of the turn.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for at least one hour
After riding for more than 8 hours

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles. They happen just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Cut their space cushions in half
Keep enough space between each rider

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space between each rider
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: In motorcycle and car crashes, how many are caused by the car driver not yielding the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: The front brake gives how much of a motorcycle's total stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other
Do both at the same time
Choose to either brake or swerve, not both
Only use the front brake, do not swerve

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve, do them one at a time. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake. Do not do both at the same time because it may cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do both at the same time

questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve, do them separately. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.
